subject: Request: Sprint nomination — Deterministic inference snapshots for Greenfield Health (pilot -> production)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Sprint nomination — Deterministic inference snapshots for Greenfield Health (pilot -> production)

Hi all,

Quick ask: Greenfield Health (pilot progressing to paid pilot, deal GFH-2027-P1) has a hard regulatory requirement that each generated response can be replayed deterministically for audit. They want per-request "deterministic snapshots" (capture request, model hash/version, prompt + system state, token-level outputs) that can be exported on demand for up to 1 year.

Why this matters: Greenfield is one of our top mid-market prospects in healthcare; closing them unlocks a 3-year reserved capacity contract and references in the sector. This is a deal-breaker in their procurement RFP.

Ask: Can Product/Eng nominate this for the next sprint or provide an explicit roadmap lane and ETA? If not, what's the minimal acceptable workaround we can promise in contract (sampled snapshots, manual export, or a runbook)? I've attached their compliance RFC and a proposed scope sheet.

Key constraints from Greenfield (excerpt):
- Immutable per-request snapshot (encrypted at rest, customer-managed KMS)
- Tamper-evident audit trail with trace IDs
- Exportable delta format (incremental, compressed)

Proposed minimal MVP (sales view):
1) Capture request + model metadata + deterministic seed and store for 90 days
2) Provide an on-demand export endpoint (manual ops for first 60 days)
3) Support CMK for export keys

I'm looping in Priyom/Laura for any customer success / legal notes I should add to the SOW.

Thanks — I need a quick yes/no by EOD Wednesday to update procurement and the customer.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0172 | connor@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Sprint nomination — Deterministic inference snapshots for Greenfield Health (pilot -> production)

Thanks for the context, Connor — good summary.

A few quick notes from product:
- We understand the business impact and the reference value. Ship-or-lose tends to be real here.
- This is not a trivial feature: it touches tracing, storage lifecycle, encryption/KMS integration, and the API surface for exports.

Could you please:
1) Confirm expected SLA for export turnaround (hours vs days)
2) Share the compliance RFC pages 3-6 where they outline tamper-evidence requirements (I see an attachment but want the exact text)
3) Confirm whether Greenfield requires snapshots for ALL requests or just a subset (e.g., PII-affecting requests)

Operational ask: Product can prepare a short spec if Eng can confirm a rough estimate. Current Eng roadmap is capacity-constrained — we have two high-impact infra projects already slated next sprint. Without an engineering nominee, we can't promise sprint inclusion.

Potential intermediate workaround we can offer in the SOW:
- Manual export service performed by Ops (paid concierge runbook) for first 90 days, with automated export targeted for Q3.

Rishi, can you comment on rough complexity (small, medium, large) and any blocking infra pieces? If we classify as "medium" we may be able to push into the next sprint if we can de-scope to sampled snapshots.

—Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: Sprint nomination — Deterministic inference snapshots for Greenfield Health (pilot -> production)

On Tue, Jun 22, 2027 at 10:04 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Rishi, can you comment on rough complexity (small, medium, large) and any blocking infra pieces?

Short answer: medium-to-large, depending on scope. Details below.

Tech dependencies and risks:
- Tracing/Trace IDs: we need deterministic trace ID propagation across load balancers and any gateway layers. Current trace stack is request-scoped; deterministic replay will require capturing the exact model RNG state (or seeding strategy) for model variants.
- Storage & retention: storing full token-level outputs at scale will increase storage by an estimated 6–12x for high-throughput customers unless we implement incremental delta compression.
- KMS/CMK: existing KMS integrations cover config, but per-tenant CMK for export keys will require policy and vault work.
- Audit tamper-evidence: we can provide HMAC chains or append-only signed manifests, but that adds crypto ops and verification code on export.

Possible mitigations (to hit a "medium" estimate):
1) Sampled snapshots (e.g., 1 in N requests) + customer attestation — reduces storage and dev scope
2) Incremental deltas + gzip for token streams — engineering effort but reduces storage footprint
3) Offer manual ops export (concierge) for the first 90 days while we scope the automated flow

Estimated effort (very rough):
- Full scope (all requests, per-tenant CMK, tamper-evidence): 6–8 engineer-sprints across infra, runtime, and security (not feasible next sprint)
- Narrow MVP (sampled snapshots, shared KMS for initial pilot, export endpoint): 2–3 engineer-sprints — could be prioritized if product narrows scope.

Action items:
- Connor: confirm whether Greenfield will accept sampled snapshots for the pilot and whether CMK is a must for go/no-go.
- Marissa/Product: prepare a 1-page spec with acceptance criteria we can estimate precisely.
- Priyom/Laura: flag any contractual language needed for a manual ops offering in the interim.

I'll block time for a 30-min sync Thurs afternoon to walk the team through the infra risks if you'd like.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Ethan Rossi <ethan.rossi@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Sprint nomination — Deterministic inference snapshots for Greenfield Health (pilot -> production)

Thanks, Connor and team — appreciate the quick follow-up.

To be explicit: for Phase 1 (pilot -> paid pilot) Greenfield can accept sampled snapshots (1 in 10) provided the sample is customer-configurable and the snapshot contains token-level output, model hash, and a signed manifest. CMK is preferred but not strictly required for pilot; we will require CMK in production.

I've attached the compliance RFC (the section I referenced is pages 3–5) and a short scope sheet. If you can agree to a manual concierge export for any ad-hoc requests during the pilot window, we can proceed with a 60-day paid pilot starting July 12.

Let me know if you need clarifications. Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow if that helps.

—Ethan Rossi
Director of Engineering, Greenfield Health
ethan.rossi@greenfieldhealth.com
